proxy.passthroughHint: When disabled, only packages already cached in this registry are served.
proxy.passthroughOverriddenByAirGap: Overridden by the Air-gapped environment setting (General tab): proxy passthrough is off while air-gapped.
proxy.osvToleranceHint: Packages with a vulnerability score above this threshold are blocked (0 – 10). Default 10 allows all.
proxy.minReleaseAgeHint: Block proxy fetches of upstream versions younger than this. Default 0 allows all. The age is measured against the upstream registry's published timestamp; versions with no upstream timestamp are allowed through.
proxy.reservedHint: Dependency-confusion guard: names matching these per-ecosystem patterns are never fetched or merged from upstream — only your hosted content serves. Names you have published are protected automatically; reserve patterns here to also cover names you haven't published yet.
proxy.installScriptAllowlistHint: Packages exempt from the install-script block gate. When the policy above is 'Block', versions listed here are served normally regardless of whether they ship an install/lifecycle script. Use this to permit known-good build tools (e.g. esbuild, node-gyp) while keeping the gate active for everything else.
proxy.blockDeprecatedHint: How upstream-deprecated versions are handled. Warn surfaces a 'deprecated' status in the UI and API. Block new refuses a deprecated version on cache miss — it is never fetched, cached, or served — while already-cached versions keep serving. Block all additionally returns 403 for already-cached versions once deprecated. Deprecation data is captured at proxy fetch and refreshed daily by the deprecation-refresh job.
proxy.blockDeprecatedBlockNew: Block new — refuse new deprecated fetches
proxy.blockDeprecatedBlockAll: Block all — also stop serving cached
proxy.blockRevokedHint: How versions removed from the upstream registry (npm unpublish, PyPI delete, a takedown of a compromised release) are handled. Detected daily by the deprecation-refresh job when a cached version no longer appears in upstream metadata; a reappearance clears it. Warn surfaces a 'revoked' badge in the UI and API while cached copies keep serving. Block returns 403 on fetch and serve and quarantines the version for review. Revoked differs from deprecated — the version is gone upstream entirely and can never be re-fetched. npm and PyPI only.
proxy.blockMaliciousHint: How versions carrying a malicious-package advisory (OSV MAL- reports from the OpenSSF malicious-packages feed, gathered by the regular vulnerability scan) are handled. These advisories usually carry no CVSS score, so the OSV score tolerance never applies to them. Block returns 403 on fetch and serve; Warn surfaces the advisory in the vulnerability report only. A per-version manual allow override still wins, as the escape hatch for false-positive reports.
proxy.blockKevHint: How versions are handled when one of their advisories aliases a CVE in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — confirmed exploited in the wild, independent of CVSS score. The catalog is refreshed daily by the threat-feed job. Block returns 403 on fetch and serve; Warn surfaces the KEV flag in the vulnerability report only. A per-version manual allow override still wins.
proxy.blockInstallScriptsHint: How versions that ship an install/lifecycle script are handled. Such a script runs automatically on install — an npm preinstall/install/postinstall hook, a PyPI sdist setup.py, or a NuGet tools install.ps1/init.ps1 or build .targets/.props. Block returns 403 on fetch and serve; Warn surfaces the badge in the version detail only. A per-version manual allow override still wins.
proxy.verifyNpmSignaturesHint: Verify the npm registry's signature on each proxied version against pinned trust anchors, the same check npm audit signatures performs. Block fails closed — a version that fails verification or carries no signature is refused (never cached or served); Warn records the outcome without blocking. Applies to proxy-fetched versions only. Configure keys in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors.
proxy.verifyNpmSignaturesNoKeys: No npm trust anchors are configured. Add the registry's SPKI public keys in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors to enable signature verification.
proxy.verifyNuGetSignaturesHint: Verify the signature embedded in each proxied .nupkg against pinned trust anchors. Block fails closed — a version whose signature fails verification or that carries no signature is refused (never cached or served); Warn records the outcome without blocking. Applies to proxy-fetched versions only. Configure certificates in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors.
proxy.verifyNuGetSignaturesNoCerts: No NuGet trust anchors are configured. Add the registry's signing certificates in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors to enable signature verification.
proxy.verifyPyPiAttestationsHint: Verify the PEP 740 digital attestation for each proxied PyPI file against pinned Sigstore roots and a Trusted Publisher allowlist. The attestation's signed digest is bound to the downloaded bytes, the Fulcio leaf is chained to a pinned root, and the publisher identity is matched. Block fails closed — a version whose attestation fails verification or that carries none is refused (never cached or served); Warn records the outcome without blocking. Applies to proxy-fetched versions only. Configure roots and publishers in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors.
proxy.verifyPyPiAttestationsNoRoots: No PyPI Sigstore roots and Trusted Publishers are configured. Add them in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors to enable attestation verification.
proxy.verifyRpmSignaturesHint: Verify the OpenPGP signature embedded in each proxied RPM package header against the org's trusted GPG keys. Block fails closed — a package whose signature fails verification or that carries none is refused (never cached or served); Warn records the outcome without blocking. Applies to proxy-fetched packages only. Requires at least one RPM trust anchor to enable.
proxy.verifyRpmSignaturesNoKey: No RPM trust anchors are configured. Add the repository's signing key in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors to enable signature verification.
proxy.verifyMavenSignaturesHint: Verify the detached OpenPGP signature (.asc sidecar) for each proxied Maven artifact against pinned trust anchors. Block fails closed — a version whose .asc fails verification or that carries none is refused (never cached or served); Warn records the outcome without blocking. Applies to proxy-fetched versions only. Configure keys in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors.
proxy.verifyMavenSignaturesNoKeys: No Maven trust anchors are configured. Add the repository's signing keys in Settings → Signatures → Trust anchors to enable signature verification.
proxy.maxEpssToleranceHint: Maximum FIRST.org EPSS exploitation probability (0.0–1.0) tolerated across a version's advisories. EPSS estimates the likelihood a CVE is exploited within 30 days; for example 0.5 blocks versions with an advisory considered more likely than not to be exploited. Scores are refreshed daily by the threat-feed job. Leave empty to disable.

upstreamRegistries.hint: Per ecosystem, the registries this proxy fetches from, in priority order. The top entry is tried first; on a miss or unreachable upstream the next is tried. Leave empty to turn symbol proxying off for this upstream.

trustAnchors.detail: These anchors were stored under an ecosystem and kind combination that has no validator, so their key material was never checked. access.title: /metrics endpoint

scrape.title: Scrape diagnostics
scrape.subtitle: Last 50 /metrics requests + lifetime allow/deny counts. Ring buffer (capacity 500); no DB hit.

tenants.empty: No tenants yet. Create one to get started.

audit.title: System audit log
audit.subtitle: Operator events only (tenant lifecycle, system_admin actions). Tenant business events are not surfaced here.

settings.title: Instance settings
settings.subtitle: Global limits and schedules — applied across every tenant.

defaults.defaultStorageQuotaBytes: unlimited (unset — no quota applied to new tenants)

metrics.title: /metrics endpoint access
metrics.subtitle: Toggle /metrics availability and configure the IP allowlist. Env vars override these values when set.
metrics.envLocked: One or more knobs are locked by env vars (METRICS_ENABLED / METRICS_ALLOWED_IPS). Unset the env var to manage via UI.
metrics.enabledHint: When off, /metrics returns 404 — the endpoint vanishes entirely (not a 403). When on, the IP allowlist controls access: source IPs on the allowlist receive 200 (anonymous), all others receive 403.
metrics.allowedIpsHint: One entry per line. Default when unset: loopback only (127.0.0.1, ::1). Examples: 10.0.0.0/8, 2001:db8::/32.
metrics.sourceIpNote: Enter IPs as the server sees the connection source. Direct Docker scrapes may appear as the Docker bridge gateway (for example 172.17.0.1) rather than the original client. To allowlist real client IPs, scrape through a trusted reverse proxy and configure TRUSTED_PROXIES.
metrics.broadCidrWarn: ⚠ 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 disables the IP gate entirely. Use only if /metrics is otherwise protected (e.g. private network, reverse-proxy auth).

recentDenied.title: Recently denied scrapes
recentDenied.hint: Connection source addresses as seen by the server, blocked by the allowlist this session. Click + Add to append to the allowlist above.
recentDenied.addTitle: Append this IP to the allowlist

slack.title: Operator Slack
slack.hint: Control-plane events only: tenant lifecycle and operator accounts. Never mirrors a per-org quarantine or vulnerability alert.
slack.webhookUrlHint: Slack incoming-webhook URL. Stored encrypted; never shown again after saving.
slack.webhookUrlRotateHint: A webhook URL is configured. Leave blank to keep it, or paste a new one to rotate it.
slack.masterKeyHint: DEPENDABLY_MASTER_KEY is not configured — set it to enable operator Slack delivery.

banners.title: System banners
banners.subtitle: Announcements shown to all authenticated users across every tenant. Banners stack in the app header and can be dismissed per user.
